RESIDUAL STRENGTH after 16 cycles at 1100 N (8 in T6.4 + 8 in T6.5 — COUNTED from the load extrema by sf9_data.n_cyc_s22, not typed; this line said 15 until 2026-08-12). ZERO-LOAD DRIFT BASELINE for T9, run FIRST in the same mounting. 928 s at 20.57 +- 0.23 N with the crosshead frozen at 0.1373 mm, so everything the DIC reports is instrument drift. Least-squares drift +0.2893 ue/s (R2 0.896) = +268 ue over the run; slope 95 pct CI +-0.0019 ue/s, so subtracting it over a 900 s hold costs only +-2 ue. Half-slopes 0.345 / 0.277 (ratio 0.80) = LINEAR, which is the drift signature; creep would decelerate. DIC NOISE FLOOR RE-MEASURED: 26 ue scatter about the trend over a full 900 s window (the +-12 ue quoted elsewhere is a 40 s window and understates long-hold noise). 9971 of 10854 rows DIC-valid. NOTE the CSV header says Infill 100 % - the specimen is 50 %; label only, no number affected.

CREEP RESOLVED - closes the T1 negative result. Held 596.55 +- 1.30 N (594.1-610.9 N) for 877 s = 7.46 MPa engineering / 11.30 MPa true on the 307.1 N anchor = 53 pct of the 21.2 MPa UTS. Raw DIC rise +1334 ue; minus the T9a drift (0.2893 ue/s x 877 s = 254 ue, 19 pct of raw) gives NET CREEP +1080 ue = 41x the 26 ue noise floor. SHAPE PASSES THE PRE-SET DISCRIMINATOR: Findley n = 0.484 (<1) and half-slopes 1.48 -> 0.59 ue/s (ratio 0.40) - decelerating primary creep, not linear drift. Creep compliance J 0.863 -> 1.008 1/GPa (+16.7 pct). Creep/instantaneous 16.8 pct is an UPPER bound (e_inst is tared at preload). To hold the load the crosshead advanced +172 um while the DIC gauge extended only +107 um, so just 62 pct of crosshead motion was specimen - the DIC channel is what makes the number right. BONUS after the policy released: fixed-grip relaxation 598 -> 582 N over 300 s (-2.8 pct). DIC 100 pct frames. E/sy/UTS/ef nulled - this is a hold, not a monotonic pull. NOTE the CSV header says Infill 100 % - the specimen is 50 %; label only, no number affected.

PETG, 100 %% infill, black spray dots. NOT A VALID PROPERTY ROW - the run was aborted at PEAK load by a false fracture trigger (a mount edge was read as a marker for one frame; ec jumped 0.029 -> 0.109 and tripped the DIC-jump branch). The specimen never fractured: it reached 2930.9 N / 36.64 MPa, then sat with the crosshead frozen for 19 s relaxing 2909 -> 2726 N. UTS/sigma_y/eps_f/toughness/anchor are all fracture-derived and were meaningless here (anchor read -2791 N off the relaxation tail), so they are nulled rather than left to be averaged in. E was 1.598 GPa on the ramp, provisional and plausible for PETG. Tracking was 100 %% - this is a control failure, not a DIC one. Redo before quoting anything.

PETG, 100 % infill. EXCLUDED from all statistics: the specimen was LOADED REPEATEDLY before it finally fractured, so the curve is not a single monotonic pull and nothing derived from it describes virgin material. The values it produced were UTS 42.87 MPa, E 1.548 GPa, eps_f 9.34 % - recorded here so they are not lost, and nulled so they cannot be averaged in. Superseded by S30/S31/S32.

STRENGTH IS VALID (UTS and sigma_y come from the load cell and never touch the DIC; UTS agrees with S30 to 2.9 %). E, eps_f and toughness are NOT - they differ from S30 by 17/51/48 %, which is the signature of the coverage, not of a different specimen. Peak 2971.1 N.

PETG, 100 % infill. Peak load 3117.5 N is SOUND (load cell) and the highest of the three PETG runs. Everything derived from stress is NOT, because the FORCE ANCHOR FAILED: the anchor is recovered from the settled post-fracture tail, which should read -(the tared-away preload) ~= -300 N, and this run's tail settled at +936 N - the specimen never fully released. analyze() therefore returned anchor -1044 N, shifting the whole stress axis down by 13 MPa and reporting UTS 25.92 instead of ~42.7. Nulled rather than left to be averaged. With the rig's usual 300 N preload assumed, UTS would be (3117+300)/80 = 42.7 MPa. Tracking 65 %. REDO, or re-derive with an explicit anchor.
